findings.title: Single long page hides task structure
findings.observation: Pairing, capture, recall, Reverie, Atlas, Attunement, Ebb, Forge, and Lore are stacked as one continuous page. Navigation names only three anchors and does not expose all implemented areas.
findings.impact: Operators must scan a long page to find work and lose context between related views.
findings.recommendation: Design a responsive application shell with explicit primary navigation, active area, selected scope, and addressable panels while preserving the current route and API actions.
findings.acceptance: Every discovered surface has an addressable navigation path and retains selected scope on desktop and handheld layouts.

findings.title: Dense controls lack grouping and hierarchy
findings.observation: Forms use inline labels, native controls, and adjacent buttons with little separation between primary and destructive actions. Reverie, Ebb, Forge, and Lore controls become visually compressed on handheld width.
findings.impact: Task intent, required inputs, and recovery actions are difficult to parse. Touch targets are visibly smaller than the configured 44px preference.
findings.recommendation: Use semantic field groups, consistent control sizing, clear primary/secondary/destructive treatments, helper text, and explicit status regions.
findings.acceptance: Representative forms meet touch-size policy, expose labels and errors, and preserve keyboard order and focus visibility.

findings.title: Status feedback is inconsistently targeted
findings.observation: Several handlers write feedback to `pair-status`, including recall and Atlas failures, instead of the status region nearest the action. Results also lack structured empty, loading, and error presentation.
findings.impact: Screen-reader and sighted users can miss the result of the action they just invoked, especially after pairing succeeds.
findings.recommendation: Give each task region its own live status and result container. Preserve response semantics and make loading, empty, error, partial, and success states explicit.
findings.acceptance: Each action announces its own result, retains user input on failure, and renders empty/error/recovery states without cross-region status leakage.

findings.title: Evidence meaning is under-explained in the rendered UI
findings.observation: The source contract requires distinctions among evidence, derivation, retrieval, inclusion, application, hypothetical output, authored Lore, and generated Lore. The current page exposes mostly raw text and IDs without a stable inspector or explanation of those meanings.
findings.impact: Users can mistake a generated summary, dream hypothesis, or retrieval hit for independently validated evidence.
findings.recommendation: Design a stable inspector and evidence badges with plain-language definitions, source/revision links, scope, uncertainty, and clear hypothetical/generated/authored distinctions.
findings.acceptance: Representative Atlas, Reverie, Lore, and Forge states show source identity, revision, provenance, uncertainty, and action consequences.

findings.title: Responsive behavior is stacking, not task reflow
findings.observation: The handheld capture is a very tall stack with controls wrapping unpredictably. There is no persistent selected scope, back path, inspector strategy, or documented narrow-state behavior.
findings.impact: Long workflows require excessive scrolling and context is easy to lose on the QR-launched handheld path.
findings.recommendation: Define desktop multi-pane and handheld stacked navigation, persistent scope, back/deep-link behavior, and deliberate reflow for forms, lists, inspectors, and dialogs.
findings.acceptance: Key journeys work at 320px reflow and 390px handheld width without horizontal overflow or loss of selected scope.

findings.title: Theme and preference lifecycle is absent
findings.observation: The page has inline light/dark color-scheme behavior but no versioned theme module, registry, settings surface, fallback, persistence, or rollback contract.
findings.impact: Visual changes cannot be safely selected, validated, persisted, or rolled back as a coherent system.
findings.recommendation: Freeze a small semantic token contract before implementation and add the host adapter only after guided direction approval. Preserve the current styling as fallback.
findings.acceptance: Theme selection is local, validated against known modules, preserves route and state, falls back on invalid selection, and has rollback evidence.

findings.title: Runtime and assistive technology coverage is incomplete
findings.observation: Desktop and handheld Chromium captures exist. Keyboard-only, screen-reader names, contrast across states, reduced motion, forced colors, and actual application interaction QA are not yet recorded.
findings.impact: The assessment cannot claim WCAG conformance or robust behavior from screenshots alone.
findings.recommendation: Run actual browser interaction and accessibility checks after design and implementation. Keep absent checks unverified, not passed.
findings.acceptance: Browser evidence covers keyboard, focus, labels, status announcements, contrast, 320px reflow, reduced motion, errors, and representative state transitions.

workerFindings.title: Primary navigation omits implemented and required work
workerFindings.acceptance: Every primary surface and Observatory status view is reachable by visible navigation at desktop and 320/390px widths.

workerFindings.title: Atlas does not carry selected context into Lore or Forge
workerFindings.acceptance: Atlas selection carries resource identity, scope, and version into Lore and Forge and survives return.

workerFindings.title: Async states lack local loading, empty, partial, and recovery presentation
workerFindings.acceptance: Each async region announces its own state, preserves input, explains partial coverage, and offers safe retry.

workerFindings.title: Dynamic preference controls lose labels and selection semantics
workerFindings.acceptance: Repeated correction inputs and selected resources have unique accessible names and current-state semantics.

workerFindings.title: Forgetting lacks confirmation, impact explanation, and recovery affordance
workerFindings.acceptance: Confirmation names target, scope, derivative impact, and external-copy limits before mutation.

workerFindings.title: Reverie loses visible job handle on reload
workerFindings.acceptance: A job deep link reloads with honest status, outputs, and only supported recovery actions.

workerFindings.title: Lore response diff is not rendered
workerFindings.acceptance: Save and refresh show scoped diffs, ownership, stale/conflict status, and authored-block preservation.

workerFindings.title: Shell is small but wire and field evidence is absent
workerFindings.acceptance: Future baseline records HAR, transfer sizes, request count, cache condition, and timing.

workerFindings.title: Authenticated and recovery paths have no runtime budget evidence
workerFindings.acceptance: Representative paired actions have response bytes, p50/p95 latency, and network recovery evidence.

workerFindings.title: Large data rendering has source-confirmed bounds risk
workerFindings.acceptance: Atlas, trace, Forge, Blueprint, Lore, and dream output have bounded pagination/rendering and visible omission semantics.
